freeze.segmented_unit_note: a segmented-unit takes neither lever the other cells take: disabled_by_script accepts the write and reads back false, so the fallback is activity_mode. Nothing else may be written to the unit afterwards — measured 2026-08-16 at 2.1.11 on this fixture, writing LuaSegmentedUnit.speed on a sleeping big-demolisher raises activity_mode from asleep to minimal in the same call and to full by the next sample, and the unit moves again. Left alone after the mode write it held asleep across 3491 ticks with its position constant to 3 decimal places, its 41 segments flat, and the corpse/smoke the waking demolisher had produced decaying to 1 and 0.
freeze.reason: owner ruling: every mobile/hostile cell is frozen and force-aligned so nothing fights, walks, dies or emits. The ruling names active=false; LuaEntity.active is READ-ONLY at 2.1.11 — measured 2026-08-16, the engine answers 'LuaEntity::active is read only.' for all 16 mobile/hostile/transient types probed — so the writable lever disabled_by_script carries the ruling instead, and every write is read back because on a segmented-unit the write is accepted and reads back false. Force alignment was already satisfied: create_entity passes force='player' for every cell (fish comes back neutral, which is the prototype's own force).
freeze.selection: the six types the ruling names, plus every other universe type that moves or fights: the three player-force turret types, land-mine, both robot types, and fish

straight-rail.reason: owner constraint: a rail segment is script-placed so infinity-cargo-wagon has something to sit on; five rails at the prototype's 2-tile pitch span 10 tiles, which covers the wagon's length inside one 26x12 cell

infinity-cargo-wagon.reason: owner constraint: the wagon is placed onto the rail segment rather than into its own cell, so it is allocated after every other cell and takes the centre rail's measured position and direction

thruster.reason: owner constraint: thrusters sit at the platform's south/bottom edge, which is where a real platform mounts them

asteroid-collector.reason: owner constraint: collectors sit at an edge with their arms facing outward, off the platform

entity-ghost.reason: a ghost of WHAT is a coverage dimension: cryogenic-plant is the richest platform-legal crafting machine measured at this pin (6 fluidboxes, 8 module slots, against chemical-plant's 4 and 3), and it is the same prototype the derivation picked to represent assembling-machine, so the ghost mirrors the fixture's richest crafter

tile-ghost.reason: a ghost of WHAT is a coverage dimension: foundation is the only tile a platform builds out of, so it is the sole tile ghost a real platform can hold

item-request-proxy.reason: a proxy is created onto an existing entity, so it is placed after every other cell and shares its target's cell; the request shape is the one tests/integration/gateway-park-proxies proves the engine accepts

character-corpse.reason: core/deserializer.lua passes inventory_size when it restores a character-corpse, so the cell must carry a non-default inventory; the stock is load-bearing — measured 2026-08-16 at 2.1.11 on this platform, an EMPTY character-corpse is culled by the engine within ~400 ticks while a corpse holding seven iron plates survives, so an unstocked cell would be gone before any export scanned it

space-platform-hub.reason: the staging platform's own hub IS the space-platform-hub cell, and the surface census confirms exactly one hub stands on the platform, so the type is in any payload the fixture produces; the premise that a SECOND hub would be refused is NOT measured — creating one was never attempted, because a hub is what makes a platform a platform and a failed attempt could cost the staging surface
